We met with the MCC and we asked if it was possible for them to reinstate the US$190 million that they had devoted to it, and they said the door is not closed. So we need to pursue that discussion."

a4634.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a4634.speech: Stressed the importance of fixing the ECG to build a resilient energy sector capable of supporting economic growth. "We want to take a look at that again because if we don't fix the ECG, we will continue to have a major problem with our whole value chain. So going ahead with privatising the last point of distribution of electricity to bring in private sector efficiency is something we want to take up again."

a4634.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a4634.speech: Revealed plans to collaborate with the World Bank for technical expertise to address inefficiencies in the energy sector, particularly losses associated with Independent Power Producers (IPPs). "The MCC grant notwithstanding, we will fall on the World Bank for the needed expertise to undertake that exercise so that we can reduce the losses where it has to do with the IPPs." ; Stated that for the short term his government's priority is to restore transparency and stabilise the energy sector through measures such as the reinstatement of the cash waterfall mechanism.

a4634.speaker: Ousmane Diagana, Regional Vice President for Western and Central Africa at the World Bank
a4634.speech: Assured Ghana of the World Bank's readiness to support the country in tackling the persistent challenges in the energy sector; described Ghana's energy sector as a long-standing concern for the World Bank, stating that it "needs fixing."

a4701.speaker: The Board of Unity Bank Plc
a4701.speech: Has announced the appointment of Ebenezer Kolawole (FCA) as the Acting Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer following the retirement of Mrs Oluwatomi Somefun who has completed her tenure as MD/CEO; the appointment was announced at the Bank’s 18th Annual General Meeting (AGM), held in Lagos on Wednesday, after securing necessary approval from its primary regulator, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).

a4736.speaker: Regina Valombola, spokesperson of the Namibian agriculture ministry
a4736.speech: Said recent FMD outbreaks in the Southern African Development Community region prompted the initiative ; “It has become imperative to raise awareness among frontline border personnel, including officials from the directorate, relevant agencies, transporters and travellers” ; said the workshop was designed to ensure all parties understand the regulations and restrictions related to the movement and importation of animals and commodities, especially during this critical period of increased disease risk.

a4767.speaker: William W. Popp, U.S. Ambassador to Uganda
a4767.speech: “It is not enough to have skilled personnel; it is important to empower them with the tools to work—the test kits/consumables that we are handing over today are part of our deliberate effort to help have as complete, timely and effective response as possible.” ; “And this is only a part of our whole of the U.S. government $4 million (over UGX 14 bn) effort on enhanced surveillance, risk communication, coordination and contact tracing.”

a4770.speaker: European Union election observer mission (statement, Tuesday)
a4770.speech: Said evidence has been found of “irregularities during counting and unjustified alteration of election results at polling station and district level” ; Is urging “the electoral bodies to conduct the tabulation process in a transparent and credible manner, ensuring the traceability of polling station results.”

a4770.speaker: Venâncio Mondlane, independent presidential candidate
a4770.speech: Blames security forces for gunning down his lawyer Elvino Dias and another political official called Paulo Guambe in the same car last Friday ; “This was a crime committed by the defence and security forces. There's no doubt about it. The special forces killed Elvino [Dias].”

a4770.speaker: Venâncio Mondlane, independent presidential candidate
a4770.speech: Has already claimed victory and alleges that the killing of his aides on Friday night was politically motivated; says the election has been stolen, and has called for further protests on Thursday and Friday.

a4770.speaker: International Republican Institute (US-based election observer mission)
a4770.speech: Vote-buying, inflated voter rolls in strongholds of the governing Frelimo party and voter intimidation have all been reported by the US-based International Republican Institute.

a4770.speaker: Mozambique's electoral commission
a4770.speech: Last month the body said its website had suffered a cyber-attack.

a4770.speaker: Local media in Mozambique
a4770.speech: Reported that across the cities of Maputo, Beira and Nampula there were multiple arrests and at least 16 people were wounded and taken to hospital.

a4770.speaker: Mia Couto, Mozambican author
a4770.speech: Has called the killings a “crime against the nation.”

a4814.speaker: EFF Gauteng member
a4814.speech: wrote following the EFF’s launch in Marikana: “In Burkina Faso they had their Thomas Sankara; Cuba had their Fidel Castro; Venezuela had Hugo Chávez; Zimbabwe had their Robert Mugabe; China had their Mao Zedong and in South Africa we have our very own young vibrant Julius Malema.”

a4814.speaker: Peter Dorrie, Think Africa Press (2012)
a4814.speech: wrote: “Four years after Sankara came to power, Burkina Faso was practically self-sufficient in its demand for basic foodstuffs. Today, the government has to import much of its food, even in years with a good harvest.”

a4814.speaker: The New York Times
a4814.speech: recalled, ten years after his death: “If Burkina Faso was unable to make material gifts to France, Mr. Sankara told his shocked French partners, the immigrants who sweep the streets of Paris for meager wages should be considered a form of reciprocal African help.”

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: demanded that cooperation agreements with former colonial power France be modified to talk of “mutual assistance” rather than aid; saw his most important project as “transform[ing] people’s attitudes”, releasing the Burkinabe from a neo-colonial mindset; was opposed to the idea of foreign aid and the financial assistance of the IMF and the World Bank: “He who feeds you, controls you.”

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: once described the modern African bourgeoisie as “passive and pathetic consumers”, who “wallow in terminology fetishised by the West just as they wallow in Western whiskey and champagne in shady-looking lounges”.

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: reportedly resigned as Information Minister in the previous government with the words “Misfortune to those who gag the people!”

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: spoke out vehemently against corruption; in 1983, addressing a rally in the capital, Ouagadougou, he complained: “The enemies of the people here inside the country are all those who have illicitly taken advantage of their social position and their place in the bureaucracy to enrich themselves. By means of bribery, manoeuvres, and forged documents, they have become shareholders in different companies.”

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: “The revolution and women’s liberation go together. We do not talk of women’s emancipation as an act of charity or because of a surge of human compassion. It is a basic necessity for the triumph of the revolution. Women hold up the other half of the sky.”

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara, President of Burkina Faso
a4814.speech: told a school in Harlem in 1984: “Our demand is not to build a world for blacks alone and against other men. As black people, we want to teach other people how to love each other.”

a4814.speaker: Andile Mngxitama, EFF leader and writer
a4814.speech: chose Sankara as the antithesis of Malema in a passionate op-ed for the Sowetan in July 2011; bemoaned the fact that Malema could have chosen to follow the path of Sankara, but had instead established himself as an “opportunist” seeking to “amass great amounts of wealth through your political influence”; accused Malema of “literally join[ing] those who stole from us to set yourself up, while the people continue to suffer”.

a4814.speaker: Andile Mngxitama, EFF leader
a4814.speech: subsequently responded aggressively on Twitter when quizzed about the fact that his own child allegedly attends a private German school.

a4814.speaker: Thomas Sankara Oath (EFF document)
a4814.speech: “As a practical indication of my acknowledgement that the only way to ensure that the services I provide are of an acceptable standard, I hereby undertake to use the services that the public sector provides to the people. What is good for me is good for the people. I therefore declare that it is a criminal offence to use private services for myself, my family and my dependents, including, but not limited to, education, healthcare, housing and transport.”

a4814.speaker: Paula Akugizibwe, writer
a4814.speech: wrote in a recent piece that “feminism was a core element of political ideology” for Sankara.

a4814.speaker: Sokari Ekrine, writer
a4814.speech: described Sankara as “meticulous in explaining class relations and the everyday ways in which African masculinities work in collaboration with capital in exploiting women’s labour and abuse of their dignity”.

a4814.speaker: EFF Manifesto
a4814.speech: states that the party is against “the oppression of anyone based on their gender, gender expression, or sexual orientation, meaning that we are against patriarchy, sexism, and homophobia in all of its manifestations”.

a4814.speaker: Floyd Shivambu, EFF leader
a4814.speech: referred to City Press journalist Carien Du Plessis as a “white bitch”, and settled the resulting lawsuit in 2012, calling it a “non-issue”.

a4814.speaker: Sipho Hlongwane, Daily Maverick
a4814.speech: asked at the time, citing a number of offensive incidents: “What is it about women that makes [Malema and Shivambu] go mental?”

a4814.speaker: Julius Malema, EFF Commander-in-Chief
a4814.speech: referred to Lindiwe Mazibuko as a tea-girl; described Helen Zille as “an ugly woman in a blue dress dancing like a monkey”; and insulted Home Affairs Minister Naledi Pandor’s accent.

a4814.speaker: Julius Malema, EFF Commander-in-Chief
a4814.speech: said in 2009 that you could tell whether a woman had been raped by her conduct the next morning, because those who had been raped would never stay for breakfast or ask for taxi money.

a4814.speaker: Julius Malema, EFF Commander-in-Chief
a4814.speech: was reported as saying, in the Caster Semenya gender controversy: “In South Africa, in the villages, we only have boys and girls. A child is a boy or a girl. They can argue about this being determined scientifically, but in the villages we don't see signs, we don't have laboratories. When a child is born, we open its legs and that is the sign we use.”

a4834.speaker: The Trump administration
a4834.speech: says it will end more than 90 percent of the U.S. Agency for International Development's foreign aid contracts.

a4834.speaker: Two immigrants sent to Guantanamo (interviewed by NPR)

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco (press conference, Monday 4 June)
a4863.speech: "For the moment, we have a level of production that cannot satisfy the demand of Afritextile, which needs between 1,500 and 2,000 tonnes of cotton per year. Following the fall in production, we have not exported any cotton since 2010" ; estimates that by 2027 cotton production will have increased sufficiently to satisfy the local market and to resume exports: "The cotton sector in Burundi is in the process of being revitalised. The process began with the government's adoption in 2019 of the national strategy for the revitalisation of Burundi's cotton-textile-clothing chain 2019-2027."

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco
a4863.speech: Reports that expected production for the 2022-2023 season is 1,500 tonnes over an area of 3,100 hectares: "At the start of the season, we forecast production of 1,800 tonnes over an area of 3,500 hectares. The planned areas were not reached because of the flooding that occurred, especially at Gatumba and in certain reserves very close to the banks of the Rusizi river" ; said the other constraints causing insufficient cotton production are the lack of fertilisers for producers, insufficient staff to supervise producers, the delay of some producers in weeding the cotton fields, which considerably reduces yields, and the insufficiency of cotton-growing land.

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco
a4863.speech: "We plan to revise upwards the price per kg of seed cotton. In the coming years we intend to calculate the price taking into account the resources invested in the crop, in order to set a remunerative price so that the farmer can recover the funds invested in production and generate a profit"; said this will motivate cotton producers, recalling that the price per kg of seed cotton has risen from 600 BIF in 2019 to 900 BIF this year.

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco
a4863.speech: Indicated that Cogerco plans to start its own cotton fields and is identifying land to be used for cotton growing: "In the past, we managed to have 8,000 hectares of cotton. But today we have fallen back to about 2,000 hectares"; castigated those who have appropriated land reserved for cotton growing in order to grow other crops there, and reported that the recovery of this land is under way.

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco
a4863.speech: Recalled that the State is the sole shareholder of Cogerco: "We have requested that an amount be set aside for cotton growing in the general State budget, but this has not yet been done"; said there need to be other investors in the sector in order to increase cotton production and contribute to the national economy.

a4863.speaker: Gustave Majambere, Director General of Cogerco
a4863.speech: Calls on cotton producers to follow closely the advice of the supervisors, and asks the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock to proceed with the effective allocation of the land already identified for cotton growing.

a4897.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4897.speech: threatened to suspend all future funding to South Africa, following accusations that the country’s new land law confiscates land and gravely discriminates against the white population; his statements, made last Sunday, announced the suspension of American aid until a full investigation into the matter is carried out.

a4897.speaker: Elon Musk, South African billionaire
a4897.speech: expressed his displeasure with the South African government’s land policies and supported Trump’s remarks on social media, describing Ramaphosa’s legislation as “overtly racist property laws.”

a4897.speaker: South African Presidency / Office of President Cyril Ramaphosa (statement)
a4897.speech: According to the South African presidency, President Ramaphosa spoke with Musk to clarify the erroneous information and distortions concerning the situation in South Africa. “During this exchange, the president recalled South Africa’s constitutional values, such as respect for the rule of law, justice, fairness and equality,” Ramaphosa’s office said in a statement on Tuesday evening.

a4897.speaker: Office of President Cyril Ramaphosa (on the expropriation law)
a4897.speech: insisted that the expropriation law is not a confiscation mechanism, but rather a legal process, enshrined in the Constitution, aimed at guaranteeing fair and equitable access to land.

a4932.speaker: Hon. Mwebesa Francis, Uganda's Minister of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives (guest of honour)
a4932.speech: emphasized the importance of supporting Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as key drivers of economic growth and job creation, particularly for East Africa's youthful population ; "We should be deliberate as the EAC region on boosting the competitiveness of MSMEs to thrive in the marketplace by supporting them to implement quality practices." ; "This will enable us to tap into the AfCFTA continental market valued at a GDP of US$2.9 trillion, with a consumer base of over 1.4 billion people."

a4932.speaker: Annette Mutaawe Ssemuwemba, EAC Deputy Secretary General for Customs, Trade and Monetary Affairs
a4932.speech: highlighted the vital role of quality in driving regional competitiveness: "Quality lies at the heart of competitiveness." ; "This ceremony is a testament to the diversity and resilience of our community, and we are grateful to the European Union for their continued support of the MARKUP II program. With a collective commitment to a culture of quality, we can unlock the full potential of our region."

a4932.speaker: Eng. James Kasigwa, UNBS (Uganda National Bureau of Standards) Executive Director
a4932.speech: noted that Uganda is actively supporting MSMEs to meet international standards as part of the country's transition from National Development Plan III to NDP IV: "Our new value proposition for growing quality MSMEs will help enhance the competitiveness of their products in both local and international markets." ; "By supporting MSMEs, we contribute to economic growth and create more employment opportunities for the region."

a4932.speaker: Adrian Njau, Executive Director of the East African Business Council (EABC)
a4932.speech: emphasized that the EAC Quality Awards represent a shared vision of fostering a robust quality culture across the region: "Studies by EABC show that adherence to quality standards results in increased intra-EAC trade, reduced border clearance time, and greater global competitiveness." ; "These awards offer MSMEs an invaluable opportunity to showcase their commitment to quality and innovation."

a4981.speaker: Erica Y Carr, USAID Acting Executive Secretary
a4981.speech: sent an email that thanked staff for clearing out classified safes and personnel documents from a Washington DC office and told them to meet in the building's lobby for an all-day disposal event on Tuesday: "Shred as many documents first, and reserve the burn bags for when the shredder becomes available or needs a break" ; the email asked staff not to overfill the burn bags and to label them with the words "SECRET" and "USAID (B/IO)" using permanent markers.

a4981.speaker: US State Department
a4981.speech: did not immediately return a request for comment.

a4981.speaker: Nikki Gamer, spokesperson, American Foreign Service Association (AFSA)
a4981.speech: told the BBC that AFSA, a union representing USAID staff, was aware employees had been asked to shred documents.

a4981.speaker: American Foreign Service Association (AFSA)
a4981.speech: said it was "alarmed" by the reports and warned that such documents "may be relevant to ongoing litigation regarding the termination of USAID employees and the cessation of USAID grants" ; noted that federal law dictates that government records must be preserved as they are "essential to transparency, accountability, and the integrity of the legal process" ; warned that "the unlawful destruction of federal records could carry serious legal consequences for anyone directed to act in violation of the law."

a4981.speaker: Kel McClanahan, executive director of the National Security Counselors
a4981.speech: said: "There is no indication in this email order that any thought is being given to proper retention or even identifying which records can be destroyed and which records cannot" ; filed a complaint with the National Archives and Records Administration, asking them to "take immediate measures" to stop the destruction of records.

a4981.speaker: The White House
a4981.speech: has argued that the agency's international programmes were a wasteful use of taxpayer dollars.

a4981.speaker: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State and acting head of USAID
a4981.speech: announced on X that the administration was cancelling "83% of the programmes at USAID" ; "The 5200 contracts that are now cancelled spent tens of billions of dollars in ways that did not serve, (and in some cases even harmed), the core national interests of the United States."

a5010.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs (via a statement of the Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
a5010.speech: Reaffirmed to Masaad Boulos Cairo's position of principle: “the unity and sovereignty of Sudan are non-negotiable”; rejected any attempt to partition the country and argued for a political process “led by the Sudanese themselves”, presented as the only credible path to a lasting peace; also called for the full implementation of the 12 September declaration of the international Quartet, which advocates an immediate humanitarian truce and a comprehensive ceasefire.

a5010.speaker: Badr Abdelatty, Egyptian Minister of Foreign Affairs
a5010.speech: In his exchange with Tom Fletcher, stressed the need to intensify international coordination in order to facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid to the worst-affected regions, and recalled his country's concrete contributions: regular relief shipments across the Egyptian-Sudanese border, the reception of refugees, and continuing cooperation with the African Union, the UN and international organisations to keep humanitarian channels open.

a5010.speaker: Masaad Boulos, adviser to the US president for Arab and Middle Eastern affairs
a5010.speech: Set out the ongoing efforts of the United States and the Quartet – made up of Washington, London, Riyadh and Abu Dhabi – to put an end to the violations in the conflict zones, particularly in Darfur.

a5010.speaker: Tom Fletcher, UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs
a5010.speech: Indicated that he would bring the “flagrant violations” committed against civilians before the Security Council, while welcoming Cairo's active role in cross-border humanitarian assistance.

a5040.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5040.speech: Rebuked the United Nations, accusing it of offering "empty words" and failing to act in the face of global conflicts, and questioned its relevance and effectiveness: "What is the purpose of the United Nations? It has such tremendous, tremendous potential, but it's not even coming close to living up to that potential. For the most part, all they seem to do is write a really strongly worded letter and then never follow that letter up. It's empty words, and empty words don't solve war. The only thing that solves wars is action."

a5040.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5040.speech: "In a period of just seven months, I have ended seven unendable wars. These include Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Israel and Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia, and Armenia and Azerbaijan."

a5040.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5040.speech: Criticised the UN for failing to assist or even acknowledge his efforts: "It's too bad that I had to do these things instead of the United Nations. In all cases, the UN did not even try to help. I never even received a phone call offering support." ; "All I got from the United Nations was an escalator that stopped halfway and a broken teleprompter."

a5080.speaker: 2023 Appropriations Act (Somalia)
a5080.speech: According to the recently approved 2023 Appropriations Act, the Armed Forces is allocated $113m, which is an increase of about $20 million for the 2022 Financial Year; Parliament allocated a paltry $115,000 to cater for orphans of SNA soldiers and the disabled, up from $53,000 in the 2022FY.

a5223.speaker: Mohamed Igueh Nour, cameraman at Radio Television of Djibouti (RTD)
a5223.speech: “Success is the sum of small efforts, repeated day after day,” he assures us enthusiastically.

a5223.speaker: Mohamed Igueh Nour, cameraman at Radio Television of Djibouti (RTD)
a5223.speech: says he acquired his knowledge and skills through his perseverance and through the support and encouragement of the men with seniority at RTD, naming Ibrahim Abdillahi Liban, Gaffar Mokhtar, Ibrahim Sy Omar and Mohamed Farah; recalls a report he produced on the French army at Baydaba in Somalia during UNOSOM in 1993.

a5412.speaker: Reliable sources in the operational theatre (anonymous)
a5412.speech: Have said this has dealt a deadly blow on the insurgents’ renewed terror campaign and that they are now desperate about escalating the situation to create the general impression that they are winning the war against the Nigerian military.

a5412.speaker: Nigerian military authority
a5412.speech: Has admitted the use of drone technology by the insurgents while attributing the development to the involvement of foreign machineries into their terror propaganda against the country: “The infiltration of foreign mercenaries in the joint operations area has significantly escalated the threat posed by terrorist groups like ISWAP and Boko Haram. The recent arrest of four Pakistani nationals which initial investigation suggested that they deal in arms running with terrorists. It suffices to mention that the foreign mercenaries facilitate tactical and strategic training for these terrorists.”

a5412.speaker: Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN)
a5412.speech: Said it is “winning the war against terrorism in the North East” and is determined to neutralize all threats, both on land and in the air, to secure the space and ensure a safe return of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes.

a5412.speaker: Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar, Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North East Operation Hadin Kai
a5412.speech: Said the “internal security situation in the North East remain still, but under control” ; “From December 2024 till date over 12 drone incidents have been recorded in the North East including the recent attack on the Cameroonian Defence Force at Ugo on the 25 March, 2025. Particularly alarming was the drone swam activities observed by troops of 25 Brigade in January this year involving 33 drones sets hovering their defensive position. Additional sitting has been reported across the sectors of the theatre operations. The drones were suspected to be conducting surveillance and aerial photography and recognizance of troop’s movement and location.”

a5412.speaker: Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar, Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North East Operation Hadin Kai
a5412.speech: Disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai killed 694 terrorists, and recovered 603 assault weapons, six 106mm bombs and 147,137 units of anti-aircraft weapons, and that troops arrested 18 serving soldiers and 15 policemen selling arms to non-state actors; maintained that the achievements were recorded under Operation Snowball, launched in August 2024 to counter ammunition racketeering, conducted across 11 states ; “So far, a total of 18 soldiers, 15 mobile policemen, and eight civilians, including a traditional ruler have been arrested. Preliminary findings from ongoing investigation reveals community pressure on serving security personnel to supply arms and ammunition for communal conflicts as driving factors.” ; “Sgt. Ameh Raphael, Armourer of 7th Division Garrison, who has been in the trade since 2018, and Sgt. Seidi Adamu of 3rd Division Ordnance Services, who has also been in the trade since 2022, had over N45 million and N34 million respectively in their accounts. Investigation also revealed that a whooping sum of N135 million was discovered to have passed through the account of a policeman, Inspector Enoch Ngwa who was arrested for arms racketeering. To this end, a more stringent punishment is necessary to act as deterrent.” ; “Additionally, a few soldiers motivated by greed are involved in ammunitions racketeering, deliberately diverting arms from the military stockpiles and supply chains to terrorists. Such actions erode battlefield morale, reduce troops’ effectiveness, and strengthen enemy resistance. The most recent incident occurred on 24th February this year when a soldier of 144 Battalion, was arrested with 30 rounds of 7.62mm specials at Tashin-Karo Kano by a military police K-19 on route search operations.” ; “Consequently, the theatre has continued to warn troops at all levels on the severe repercussions and sanctions of ammunition racketeering. Those found culpable have been dismissed and handed over to the police to serve as deterrent.”

a5412.speaker: Major General Abdulsalam Abubakar, Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North East Operation Hadin Kai
a5412.speech: Emphasized that “From January 2025 to the date, over 186 terrorist logistics suppliers, spies and collaborators have been arrested across the theatre of operation. However, a lack of tracking device has continued to mitigate the arrest of logistic suppliers. Another point of concern is the observed increase in cases of collusion by some non-governmental organizations who convey additives and food items to terrorist locations under the guise of humanitarian assistance.” ; lamented the activities of fifth columnists which undermines the overall success of Operation Hadin Kai.

a5412.speaker: Major Darush Yusuf, Acting Commander, Forward Operating Base (FOB) Molai
a5412.speech: Said they have been experiencing Boko Haram drone activities at Molai, but anytime they sight them, they bring them down, and noted that troops have superior weapons that take down Boko Haram drones before they get close to their location: “We sight their drones from afar and take them down before they near our troop’s location. We don’t miss the target. I won’t disclose the weapon we use for security reasons. But their drones don’t pose serious threat to us at FOB Molai. You know we are at the middle between the Sambisa forest and Timbukto Triangle. From Molai to Kumala, the Boko Haram crossing point from Sambisa to Timbukto is not far.”

a5412.speaker: Major Darush Yusuf, Acting Commander, Forward Operating Base (FOB) Molai
a5412.speech: Stated that their mode of operation at FOB Molai is a “do-or-die-affair”: “We don’t sleep here, because it is a 24 hours operation. We don’t wait for them, we go for them. We are the last defensive line for the Nigerian military. We have been given everything we need to fight this war and we are grateful for that. Our equipment is 100 percent and all the soldiers here are happy with their welfare from the Nigerian Army. We have continued to record huge successes. Few days ago, following intelligence, we engaged and neutralized terrorists at their crossing point in Kumala to Sambisa forest where we recovered six 106mm howitzer bombs.”

a5412.speaker: Brigadier General Mohammed Abu-Mawashi, team lead
a5412.speech: Said in his opening remarks that the media tour was the brain child of the Chief of Defence Staff, General Christopher Musa, which aimed at giving Defence Correspondents the rare opportunity to interact with frontline formations and units, so as to tell the true picture of what the military was doing.

a5453.speaker: China / Chinese leaders (National People's Congress plan)
a5453.speech: China has set an economic growth target for this year of “around 5%” and pledged to pump billions of dollars into its ailing economy, which is now facing a trade war with the US. Its leaders unveiled the plan as thousands of delegates attend the National People's Congress.

a5588.speaker: 2013 academic report
a5588.speech: Cited as the source for the finding that the elephant population in the region has dropped by 62% in the last decade.

a5588.speaker: WWF
a5588.speech: Cited as the source for the estimate that Botswana has some 150,000 elephants, the biggest population in Africa, continuing to grow by 5% annually.

a5588.speaker: Conservation groups
a5588.speech: Celebrated Botswana’s December 2013 ban on trophy hunting on state land, saying it would put pressure on neighbouring countries to take the same action.

a5588.speaker: CITES
a5588.speech: In 2013 singled out Kenya and Tanzania as part of its ‘Gang of 8’ problematic countries, criticising them for lacking any semblance of a competent national action plan to combat the rampant poaching; the ‘Gang of 8’ has recently swelled to a total of 19 countries identified by CITES as lacking national action plans to combat poaching, including Uganda, Angola, Cameroon, Congo, DRC, Egypt, Ethiopia, Gabon, Mozambique and Nigeria.

a5588.speaker: Interpol
a5588.speech: Has identified Kenya and Tanzania as major source and transit countries in the illegal ivory trade.

a5588.speaker: Kenyans United Against Poaching, a consortium of community groups
a5588.speech: Gathered 20,000 signatures to encourage Kenyan President Uhuru Kenyatta to declare poaching a national disaster.

a5588.speaker: Kenyan Ministry of Environment and Kenyan Wildlife Services (KWS), via the Standard newspaper
a5588.speech: Have hit back with what can only be described as dangerous claims that poaching has not led to diminished elephant populations, and that calling the current situation a disaster is likely to scare off tourists.

a5588.speaker: Retired KWS game warder (interview with the Standard)
a5588.speech: Listed staffing issues, poor leadership and resource constraints as reasons for the KWS anti-poaching unit’s lack of success, and argued that instead of indulging the tendency of the Kenyan government to “argue about carcasses”, it would be more productive to identify where improvements can be made and direct resources towards those improvements.

a5588.speaker: Wildlife Direct study
a5588.speech: Cited as the source for the finding that only 7% of those convicted of elephant and rhino-related crimes actually served prison time between 2008 and 2013.

a5588.speaker: James Lembeli, Chairman of the Tanzanian Parliamentary Committee on Land, Natural Resources and Environment
a5588.speech: Has claimed that senior government officials in departments responsible for wildlife conservation are directly involved in poaching activities, and argues this is why anti-poaching campaigns in the country have so far been ineffective.

a5588.speaker: Government of Tanzania
a5588.speech: In response to international pressure, committed earlier this year to “place beyond economic use” its stockpile of ivory, valued at approximately US$50 million, but has yet to do so and has offered no explanation as to why it has not.

a5600.speaker: Authorities in Fashoda County, Upper Nile State
a5600.speech: Are urgently appealing for humanitarian assistance after the recent flooding affected over 1,200 households and impacted more than 8,000 people.

a5600.speaker: Sabino Onyot, Coordinator of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Kodok
a5600.speech: Said the flood devastated three key areas - Lul, Dethouk, and Kodok - where homes, schools, health facilities and churches were submerged and destroyed; adds that the displaced people have sought refuge on higher ground in various parts of Fashoda County and stresses that the community is in urgent need of food, shelter, and medical assistance ; "We have several Payams affected by the flood, and many people have migrated to Lul Payam for shelter. In Lul Payam alone, 500 households have been impacted" ; "The affected population in Lul Payam includes host community members, returnees, and internally displaced persons (IDPs), with a total of around 3,000 people" ; "In Dethouk Payam, we have recorded 249 affected households" ; "Lastly, in Kodok Payam, which is one of Fashoda's four Payams, 492 households, or roughly 1,194 individuals, have been affected by the floods" ; confirmed that since the displacement, there have been 23 reported cases of snake bites in the affected areas.

a5676.speaker: Rory McIlroy, golfer, Masters champion
a5676.speech: “Physically I feel like my game is there, it is just mentally getting myself in the right frame of mind to get the best out of myself”, McIlroy said after his 67 at Oakmont last Sunday ; “I climbed my Everest in April and I think after you do something like that you’ve got to make your way back down and look for another mountain to climb.”

a5676.speaker: Rory McIlroy, golfer, Masters champion
a5676.speech: “I’ve earned the right to do whatever I want to do”, he said (in the context of his dealings with the media).

a5676.speaker: Collin Morikawa, golfer
a5676.speech: He later said: “I don’t owe anyone anything”, after blanking reporters following his loss at the Arnold Palmer Invitational at Bay Hill in March.

a5688.speaker: Senior executives of the Ministry of Women and the Family (MFF), Djibouti
a5688.speech: Each in turn set out the rationale and objectives of the CASAF, describing it respectively as a “school of the second chance” and a “centre of reference” in the socio-professional integration of Djiboutian young girls in difficulty.

a5720.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the Operation Recover All the Loot (ORAL) Committee and MP for North Tongu
a5720.speech: Has underscored the need for legislation to prevent political appointees and exposed persons from acquiring state assets; said the law would prevent a future occurrence of the acquisition of state property by private and politically exposed persons.

a5720.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the ORAL Committee
a5720.speech: Reiterated the commitment of ORAL to recover state assets and fight corruption, dismissing claims that its efforts were merely a "flash in the pan" or a political gimmick; said the work of the committee was multifaceted and far-reaching, with several phases designed to ensure that justice was served; explained that its current phase focused on gathering evidence and compiling data, which would be followed by confiscations, retrievals, recoveries, prosecutions and further investigations; said the committee's efforts were also expected to lead to reforms, including legislation prohibiting politically exposed persons from purchasing state assets and changes to how the Lands Commission valued state assets. ; "The Ghanaian people want to see the end of this. They want us to get to the bottom."

a5720.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the ORAL Committee
a5720.speech: Assured the affected CSIR staff of their protection and safety, adding that they would not be ejected and that their issue would be included in the report to the President.

a5720.speaker: Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, Chairman of the ORAL Committee
a5720.speech: Described the situation as a 'state capture' and attributed it to the "insatiable greed" of political appointees and politically-exposed persons; also commended President Mahama's directive to halt all land transactions, describing it as timely and crucial.

a5720.speaker: ORAL team
a5720.speech: Told journalists that the CSIR staff bungalows have been sold to a private developer with ties to the previous government but are yet to be demolished, and that the tenants have been served with ejection notices since December 30, 2024.

a5720.speaker: Raymond Archer, former investigative journalist and ORAL committee member
a5720.speech: Reiterated that the visit was to validate petitions and concerns about appropriation of state property to private and politically exposed persons: "We are here today as you have witnessed to go through side by side to see whether indeed what is contained in the petition actually exists or not. You have seen it for yourselves. You can draw your own conclusions about what has happened in the past. As far as we are concerned, we are going to include this in our report to the President and further action will surely be taken on these issues." ; "You've seen public officials that are actively working for the state being ejected from their homes to make way for private interest and also interests that are connected to other public officials. This is obviously what our President campaigned against and you are witnesses to what has happened."

a5809.speaker: Patricia Mahoney, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5809.speech: “AIDS is a common enemy to all. It has no borders and spares no one” ; explains that the fight against HIV infections and the AIDS epidemic is among the priorities of United States cooperation, the largest contributor to the fund for the global response to the AIDS epidemic, but that because of stigma and discrimination efforts are still needed to reach key populations, particularly sex workers.

a5809.speaker: Patricia Mahoney, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5809.speech: welcomes the successes recorded and the contribution the Dindji project has made to improving the social and legal environment and access to quality care by key populations in Benin and Togo; particularly appreciated the training of 504 health workers in non-discrimination; praised the testing of key populations and the referrals and management of positive cases; stresses that these results would not have been achieved without the implementing partner OCAL, in collaboration with the National AIDS Control Programme (CNLS-TP), and acknowledged the contributions of partner NGOs such as Besyp, Cérid, Sidaction, Racines and Solidarité.

a5809.speaker: Patricia Mahoney, Ambassador of the United States of America to Benin
a5809.speech: Her wish is that the results and good practices of the Dindji project be taken up by the national bodies in charge of the fight against new HIV infections, so that no target group is left aside; ending the epidemic means progress in respect for civil, economic, political, social, sexual and reproductive rights, and defending the rights of sex workers is fundamental to guaranteeing their access to life-saving services without discrimination.

a5809.speaker: Pétas E. Akogbéto, Chief of Staff of the Minister of Health of Benin
a5809.speech: For him, the project has made, in view of its results, a decisive contribution towards reaching the target; he announced that the closure of this project will be followed by another project to support the government's efforts in the fight against HIV/AIDS in Benin.

a5810.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a5810.speech: has once again expressed his deep concern about the deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the Tindouf refugee camps; in his latest report he said he was worried about the serious consequences of the surge in food prices, which disproportionately affects the Sahrawi populations ; “This situation, combined with extreme climatic conditions and a lack of economic opportunities, is plunging many Sahrawis into a state of malnutrition and great vulnerability.”

a5810.speaker: UN Secretary-General's report
a5810.speech: highlights serious human rights violations, including malnutrition, which causes illnesses such as anaemia among children, pregnant women and other camp inhabitants.

a5810.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General (2024 report)
a5810.speech: noted that the food security assessment reported a “deterioration of conditions in the camps”, due to a 30% reduction in dry food rations attributable to the rise in prices; according to this assessment, more than 80% of camp inhabitants now depend on food aid.

a5810.speaker: Former members of the Polisario Front (testimonies)
a5810.speech: indicate that only 20% of camp residents are of Sahrawi origin, while the rest would be made up of people from various tribes, notably Algerian.

a5810.speaker: Sahrawi NGOs
a5810.speech: have documented cases of mismanagement and diversion of resources, implicating Polisario officials in collaboration with the Algerian authorities.

a5820.speaker: Mohamed Mchengerwa, Minister of State in the President’s Office for Regional Administration and Local Government (TAMISEMI)
a5820.speech: Concluded the Local Government Elections on November 29, 2024 by announcing the winners in that election of chairpersons of streets, villages and hamlets.

a5820.speaker: Members and supporters of Chama cha Mapinduzi (CCM)
a5820.speech: For CCM members and supporters, the results (in which the party was declared to have won 99 percent) demonstrated the great support for its policies among Tanzanians.

a5820.speaker: Critics, including the opposition parties
a5820.speech: Claim the results came from foul play which CCM, in collaboration with state organs, especially the Police Force, carried out throughout the entire electoral exercise; these fouls, they claim, include the arbitrary disqualification of opposition candidates, the denial of letters to their agents, the presence of fake ballots, and violence and chaos against opposition candidates.

a5820.speaker: Some commentators (on the child-disappearance reports)
a5820.speech: Tried to show that whenever an election arrives, these incidents of children disappearing flourish, with the suspicion that those who have declared their intention to run for office are behind these incidents in order to strengthen their chances of victory.

a5820.speaker: Some Tanzanians
a5820.speech: Have appealed to President Samia Suluhu Hassan to intervene and correct the situation of abductions.

a5820.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Vice Chairman of CHADEMA (Tanzania Mainland)
a5820.speech: Wants the party to stir up the drive and enthusiasm of members and of Tanzanians so that they can rise up and reject this situation, appearing to disparage and belittle what is called "reconciliation" between CHADEMA and CCM.

a5820.speaker: Freeman Mbowe, Chairman of CHADEMA
a5820.speech: Has made clear his intention to defend his position; does not appear to see the importance of using "people power" to confront CCM’s "authoritarianism," but rather encourages, and defends, the approach of reconciliation.

a5820.speaker: Court of Tanzania (ruling in the Nawanda case)
a5820.speech: The Court said there was not sufficient evidence to prove that Nawanda had committed the offence with which he was charged, after which he was set free.

a5857.speaker: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) latest results
a5857.speech: Indicate that over 2 million people are currently food insecure (IPC 3+) in Mozambique (April-September 2025), projected to increase to 2.6 million during the lean season (October 2025 - March 2026), including over 170,000 people classified as severely food insecure (IPC Phase 4), with protracted conflict, three consecutive cyclones in the north and considerable food price increases continuing to drive food insecurity; the average prevalence of acute malnutrition among children aged 6-59 months in the post-shock period is estimated at 4 percent, with approximately 115,000 children under 5 and over 29,000 pregnant or breastfeeding women requiring treatment during the lean season.

a5857.speaker: WFP Mozambique (Emergency Response External Situation Report, 18 August 2025)
a5857.speech: Reports that the security situation in Cabo Delgado has sharply deteriorated since the end of the rainy season in April, with over 57,000 people displaced between 28 July and 3 August after attacks by Non-State Armed Groups in Ancuabe, Chiure and Muidumbe, and that WFP and partners are stepping up to assist, with over 30,000 newly displaced people reached with 15-day food rations in Chiure under the Joint Response Programme (with IOM, UNICEF and UNHCR); operations in Quissanga were suspended on 05 August due to reported NSAG presence and distributions in Macomia rely solely on stock available in the district.

a5857.speaker: WFP Mozambique (Emergency Response External Situation Report, 18 August 2025)
a5857.speech: States that for the next six months (September 2025 - February 2026) WFP needs USD160 million to continue its activities in the country, that regular food assistance in the north and nutrition programmes are heavily underfunded, that humanitarian operations in conflict-affected Cabo Delgado are critically underfunded with another reduction in the number of people assisted planned for November if no additional resources are confirmed, that for the cyclone response WFP secured funds to assist only some 200,000 of the over 470,000 people targeted, and that the Drought Appeal has secured only USD 33 million (15 percent) of the required USD 222 million.

a5857.speaker: WFP Mozambique (Emergency Response External Situation Report, 18 August 2025)
a5857.speech: Reports that for the July-August distribution cycle WFP reduced the caseload for regular humanitarian assistance in Cabo Delgado from 420,000 to 344,000 people due to limited resources, warning that the impact of disrupted assistance could force many to adopt harmful coping mechanisms such as early marriage and child labour, which could exacerbate intercommunal tensions in fragile contexts and increase the likelihood of violence.

a5857.speaker: WFP Mozambique (Emergency Response External Situation Report, 18 August 2025)
a5857.speech: Reports that in Nampula WFP delivered food assistance to over 62,000 people affected by Cyclone Jude in Mossuril and Ilha de Mocambique through value vouchers and cash transfers; that drought (El Nino) distributions in central and southern Mozambique finished in July with over 250,000 people reached since November 2024, with nutrition assistance continuing; that over 8,700 students were reached with take-home rations in Caia district under the School Feeding in Emergency and Recovery Programme; and that WFP supported the government's drought anticipatory action, assisting 180,000 people with cash-based transfers and supporting INGD to assist 1,000,000 people with asset creation activities.

a5896.speaker: Felix Nkulukusa, Zambian Secretary to the Treasury
a5896.speech: Says cooperating partners have responded positively now that Government has outlined specific measures to mitigate the impact of the drought.

a5896.speaker: Felix Nkulukusa, Zambian Secretary to the Treasury
a5896.speech: Speaking to prospective investors at the JP Morgan-hosted meeting on Zambia’s economic and monetary policy outlook, said the country has learnt key lessons from the debt-restructuring battlefield process; said Zambia is on the way to achieving full fiscal sustainability while preserving social sector spending for those in need; said the country is reforming the Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) to improve domestic resource mobilisation and tighten control of expenditure while improving cash management ; “On the drought situation that has affected hydro-power generation, the mines have agreed to pay higher charges for imported power because they don’t want to reduce production but the challenge is that the entire region is affected and there is nowhere to import required quantities.”

a5896.speaker: Denny Kalyalya, Bank of Zambia Governor
a5896.speech: Said despite recent headwinds regarding rising inflation and fluctuations in the forex market, Zambia’s growth outlook is still very promising with the economy projected to grow by over five percent in 2028 ; “We have had challenges with inflation and depreciation of the currency due to elevated maize and fuel prices and low inflows of FX, mainly from the mines that recorded low production.” ; “But we expect FX inflows to increase with the revamping of operations at Mopani and Konkola Copper Mines and the outlook for copper prices is positive.”

a6013.speaker: Rami Khouri, American University of Beirut
a6013.speech: Stressed that Arab governments and their external sponsors tend to prioritize the wrong threats; that most Arab governments continue to introduce superficial reforms in pivotal sectors such as education, employment, and anti-corruption, but their efforts mostly remain unsuccessful or limited in their impact, while the broader Arab trend since the end of the Cold War around 1990 sees steadily increasing pauperisation, vulnerability, perceived injustice and helplessness, and disparities.

a6013.speaker: Rami Khouri, American University of Beirut
a6013.speech: Said the symptoms of the systemic crisis started to appear several decades ago and could have been alleviated much more easily at the outset had governments been more effective in recognizing and tackling corruption, insufficient decent jobs, state cronyism, and declining educational standards; instead regimes focused on military security and internal repression, which contributed to the brisk emigration of educated youth, the collapse of political parties, the rise of sectarian groups and militias, and steady expansion in adherents to both nonviolent and militant Islamist movements.

a6013.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail, 2018 study "Poverty and Vulnerability in Arab States"
a6013.speech: Stated that the actual levels of poverty and vulnerability in the Arab region are higher than previously thought, with some two-thirds of citizens falling into the categories of poor or vulnerable, and that the realities of declining family wellbeing were disguised by prevailing poverty measures based on daily expenditures.

a6013.speaker: Economists at UNDP, the UN Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA), the World Bank and other institutions (Multi-Dimensional Poverty research)
a6013.speech: Their Multi-Dimensional Poverty figures indicate poverty rates as much as four times higher than previously assumed; if the level of 66 percent poor/vulnerable holds for the entire Arab world, some 250 million people may be poor or vulnerable out of a total Arab population of 400 million.

a6013.speaker: ESCWA economists
a6013.speech: According to ESCWA economists who have analyzed this issue, the middle class in non-oil-producing states has shrunk from 45 percent to 33 percent of the population; they see many middle income families sliding into vulnerability, and vulnerable families in turn falling into poverty.

a6013.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a6013.speech: Noted that the drivers of this increase in poverty and vulnerability have persisted or worsened since the 2010-11 Arab uprisings and are likely to drive further families into poverty and vulnerability for years to come.

a6013.speaker: Khalid Abu-Ismail
a6013.speech: Further argued that this trend seems to be directly associated with the steady recent decline in the quality of state-managed basic social services, mainly outside the Gulf region, including health care, education, water, electricity, transport, and social safety nets.

a6013.speaker: ESCWA (calculations)
a6013.speech: The number of Arabs requiring humanitarian assistance to stay alive and minimally healthy, according to ESCWA calculations, is 60 million people in seven crisis states, including many of the 30 million people who have been displaced in the Arab region in recent years.

a6013.speaker: 2019 MENA Economic Monitor report
a6013.speech: Indicated that once families fall into poverty, they are likely to remain there for generations to come.

a6013.speaker: IMF and other projections
a6013.speech: Say the Arab region must create 60-100 million jobs by 2030, and 27 million jobs in the next five years, to reduce unemployment significantly.

a6071.speaker: Sylvia Opinia, WHO PRS Coordinator (represented by Dr. Inigbehe Oyinloye, WHO PRS Technical Officer)
a6071.speech: Revealed that the participants cut across 7 recognized Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) in the state and will be supported to conduct 8 weeks of community engagement activities across 6 selected local government areas (Fika, Potiskum, Nangere, Nguru, Damaturu, and Bade) ; “This capacity building is to increase awareness of GBV, its consequences, and the role of health workers in supporting survivors in the context of meningitis response. It is also aimed at creating awareness of PRSEAH (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Harassment) and its reporting among the communities, as well as to break the culture of silence and address the stigmatization of survivors” ; explained the training will be integrated with key messages of meningitis to increase awareness and improve across the CSO's LGAs of assignment.

a6071.speaker: Dr. Lawan Gana, Yobe State Commissioner for Health (represented by Abdullahi Danchuwa, Executive Secretary of Yobe State Emergency Medical and Ambulance Services and Chairman of Sexual Assault Referral Centres)
a6071.speech: Explained a total of over 1,000 cases of GBV were recorded in the year 2023 alone ; “As I welcome you to this capacity building on behalf of Commissioner for Health, Dr. Lawan Gana who could not come here in person due to tight schedules, being members of the Civil Society Organisations, you play a very significant role in watching over what happens in your society” ; “Yobe state government has zero tolerance for GBV in the state and we will continue to partner with you in ensuring the cases of GBV are reduced to its barest minimum because over 1,000 cases of the crime were recorded within the state in the year 2023 alone.” He also charged them not to be found wanting in discharging their duties as doing so would jeopardize the successes recorded in the last few years.

a6098.speaker: Salah Ahmed Jama, Deputy Prime Minister of the Federal Government of Somalia
a6098.speech: Addressing the assembled stakeholders, Deputy Prime Minister Jama articulated the project's critical importance to the nation's future. He described JOSP as a national priority and a central pillar of Somalia's National Transformation Plan (2025-2029).

a6119.speaker: Mikatekiso Kubayi, researcher in international relations at the Institute for Global Dialogue, UNISA
a6119.speech: Observes that “the unipolarity of the old world is fading”; explains that Washington recognises this “new reality” and is trying to protect its interests, looking back at the latest round of Russian-American negotiations in Riyadh; indicates that the rise of powers such as Russia, India, China and Brazil challenges the traditional dominance of the United States; concludes: “For now, the question is what the nature or character of this multipolarity would be. And that is something the global community must negotiate and decide.”

a6245.speaker: United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF)
a6245.speech: Has warned that more than 80,000 children are at high risk of contracting cholera as the rainy season intensifies across West and Central Africa; said in a new report that the heightened risk is being driven by ongoing cholera outbreaks in Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, raising the likelihood of cross-border transmission to neighbouring countries.

a6245.speaker: Muhammad Pate, Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare of Nigeria
a6245.speech: Explained that 274 projects have been executed across 35 tertiary hospitals in northern Nigeria, serving over 4.5 million outpatients and 1.6 million inpatients; noted that the commitment of the President Bola Tinubu administration to improving national health outcomes is being matched with action, with the provision of health infrastructure across all levels of healthcare delivery nationwide.

a6245.speaker: National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a6245.speech: Announced plans to expand healthcare access for newborns by incorporating neonatal care into its flagship Financing Access to Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmOC) programme.

a6245.speaker: Kelechi Ohiri, Director-General of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA)
a6245.speech: Said the maternal health component of the programme, launched nearly a year ago, had already delivered life-saving interventions to over 6,000 vulnerable women with obstetric complications nationwide, and said that building on this progress the scheme is now shifting focus to the often-overlooked neonatal population.

a6245.speaker: Health experts, policymakers and private innovators at the third Insights Learning Forum (ILF) in Abuja
a6245.speech: Renewed calls for local investment and intentional digital innovation to address Nigeria’s long-standing primary healthcare crisis, with a cross-sector consensus that meaningful change must begin at the local level and be driven by Nigerians.

a6245.speaker: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
a6245.speech: Issued a nationwide health alert over the rising threat of waterborne and vector-borne diseases, warning of a surge in cholera, yellow fever and dengue fever cases, especially in states already experiencing floods and heavy rainfall.

a6245.speaker: Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) impact-based weather forecast
a6245.speech: Identified Sokoto, Kaduna, Zamfara, Yobe and several other states as facing heightened risk of flooding throughout July.

a6245.speaker: US government
a6245.speech: Says PEPFAR has provided life-saving antiretroviral treatment and healthcare support to more than 25 million people worldwide.

a6245.speaker: Olutomi Sodipo, State Project Manager of the Philanthropic Funding Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (PF SMC) in the FCT
a6245.speech: Disclosed during a press conference in Abuja that the FCT aims to reach 983,497 children in 2025 with Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention, and said the intervention targeted children aged three to 59 months, those most vulnerable due to weaker immune systems.

a6245.speaker: Jean Kaseya, Director-General of the Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a6245.speech: Described climate change as one of the most pressing public health challenges of our time, speaking during the official launch of the framework; said climate change is already wreaking havoc across Africa, driving extreme weather events, shifting disease patterns, food insecurity and waterborne illnesses; and said that, according to a review of over 2,000 public health events on the continent between 2001 and 2021, 56 per cent were linked to climate change.

a6245.speaker: Godwin Ntadom, Director of Public Health at the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare
a6245.speech: Said that through collective efforts Nigeria continues to record steady progress in the fight against Onchocerciasis and Lymphatic Filariasis; noted that transmission of Lymphatic Filariasis has been interrupted in 379 LGAs while the Onchocerciasis Elimination Programme has halted disease transmission in nine states and completely eliminated the disease in two.

a6245.speaker: Association of Nigerian Private Medical Practitioners (ANPMP)
a6245.speech: Said that private medical practitioners currently attend to about 70 to 80 per cent of Nigerian patients.

a6245.speaker: Kay Adesola, President of the Association of Nigerian Private Medical Practitioners (ANPMP)
a6245.speech: Said private medical doctors are committed to enhancing the treatment of emergency cases nationwide, aiming to significantly reduce fatalities during critical health situations, and emphasised the association’s desire to manage all emergencies, highlighting private medical facilities as the primary “round-the-clock life-saving” entities within the health sector.

a6269.speaker: Hassan Mohamed Hussein Mungaab, Governor of Banadir Region and Mayor of Mogadishu
a6269.speech: Has revealed that while the Banadir Regional Administration pays salaries to 3,000 employees, fewer than 600 are actually working; described the situation as “massive corruption” crippling the administration ; “Three thousand employees are on the Banadir Regional Administration payroll, but if you check today, fewer than 600 can be found working at the municipal headquarters” (during a meeting with Banadir staff on Saturday, August 9, 2025) ; stressed his desire for all employees to report to work, but acknowledged a major obstacle: many of those listed as municipal staff are not actually employed by the city.

a6269.speaker: Hassan Mohamed Hussein Mungaab, Governor of Banadir Region and Mayor of Mogadishu
a6269.speech: Added that his administration has been informed that some international aid previously received will soon be cut; warned that some international aid to the federal government will be cut by the end of this year: “You know there is concern that in the coming years – or even by the end of this year – as I discussed with the Minister of Health, we cannot be certain donors will continue their support for the health sector. Therefore, it is important we take precautions now and take control of our own activities.”

a6269.speaker: Sources in the Banadir Administration’s Department of Labor (anonymous)
a6269.speech: Told Kaab TV that ministers and senior government officials have added their children and spouses to the payroll despite them doing no work.

a6269.speaker: Kaab TV
a6269.speech: Has learned that the list includes social media influencers of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, as well as relatives of the intelligence chief Mahad Salaad and Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, none of whom reside in Somalia or perform any civil service duties.

a6269.speaker: Transparency International
a6269.speech: According to Transparency International, Somalia ranks as the most corrupt country in the world.

a6321.speaker: Imam Fuad Adeyemi, National Chief Imam of Al-Habibiyyah Islamic Society
a6321.speech: Has urged Muslims to unite in building a self-sustaining charitable organisation to support the needy ; speaking in Abuja during an inter-faith interaction on philanthropy, said Islamic organisations must strengthen the use of waqf (endowment) to provide organised funding for poverty alleviation ; said traditional charities are overstretched due to global economic crises, citing recent cuts by international agencies such as USAID ; "Muslims are the source of philanthropy. We have waqf. Let's revive it to create an organisation that will help the entire world."

a6321.speaker: Malam Abdulrahman Alalubosa
a6321.speech: Said endowments have historically sustained communities, with wealthy Muslims donating farms and houses for public welfare ; urged greater adoption of "cash waqf," where pooled funds can be invested in halal businesses, with profits channelled to widows, orphans and the poor.

a6321.speaker: Malam Abdulrahman Alalubosa
a6321.speech: Further advised the government to encourage Zakat (compulsory almsgiving) through tax deductions, as practiced in Malaysia, and ensure proper legal backing for transparent disbursement.

a6321.speaker: Other speakers at the inter-faith interaction on philanthropy
a6321.speech: Said a coordinated, faith-based charity system would enhance social welfare and reduce dependence on foreign aid.

a6368.speaker: Mediators (Qatar, Egypt and the US, announcement in Doha)
a6368.speech: Israel and Hamas agreed to a ceasefire deal, mediators announced Wednesday, pausing a devastating 15-month war in the Gaza Strip and raising the possibility of winding down the deadliest and most destructive fighting between the bitter enemies.

a6368.speaker: Three US officials and one Hamas official (anonymous)
a6368.speech: Three officials from the U.S. and one from Hamas confirmed that a deal had been reached. All three U.S. officials and the Hamas official requested anonymity to discuss the contours of the deal before the official announcement by mediators in Doha.

a6368.speaker: Senior Israeli official (anonymous)
a6368.speech: said details are still being ironed out.

a6368.speaker: Officials (unnamed)
a6368.speech: U.S. President Joe Biden was preparing to address the breakthrough agreement later Thursday, officials said.

a6368.speaker: Local health officials (Gaza)
a6368.speech: Israel responded with a fierce offensive that has killed over 46,000 Palestinians, according to local health officials. They do not distinguish between civilians and militants but say women and children make up more than half of those killed.

a6368.speaker: U.N. and international relief organizations
a6368.speech: estimate that some 90% of Gaza’s 2.3 million people have been displaced, often multiple times. They say tens of thousands of homes have been destroyed and hospitals are barely functioning.

a6368.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a6368.speech: Experts have warned that famine may be underway in northern Gaza, where Israel launched a major offensive in early October, displacing tens of thousands of residents.

a6368.speaker: Abed Radwan, Palestinian father of three displaced from Beit Lahiya
a6368.speech: “The best day in my life and the life of the Gaza people,” Abed Radwan said of the ceasefire deal. “Thank God. Thank God.” Radwan, who has been displaced from the town of Beit Lahiya for over a year and shelters in Gaza City, said he will try to return to his hometown, and “rebuild my house, and rebuild Beit Lahiya.” He spoke to AP over the phone. His voice has been overshadowed by celebrations. “People are crying here. They don’t believe it’s true.”

a6368.speaker: Sharone Lifschitz, daughter of hostage Oded Lifschitz
a6368.speech: told the AP by phone she was stunned and grateful but won’t believe it until she sees them come home.

a6368.speaker: Joe Biden, US President
a6368.speech: Biden, who has provided crucial military aid to Israel but expressed exasperation over civilian deaths, announced the outline of the three-phase ceasefire agreement on May 31. ; He said the first phase would last for six weeks and include a “full and complete ceasefire,” a withdrawal of Israeli forces from densely populated areas of Gaza and the release of a number of hostages, including women, older adults and wounded people, in exchange for the release of hundreds of Palestinian prisoners. Humanitarian assistance would surge, with hundreds of trucks entering Gaza each day.

a6368.speaker: Hamas
a6368.speech: had been demanding assurances for a permanent end to the war and complete withdrawal of all Israeli forces from Gaza. ; Hamas has threatened anyone who cooperates with Israeli forces.

a6368.speaker: Israel (government)
a6368.speech: has repeatedly said it would not halt the war until it destroys Hamas’ military and governing capabilities.

a6368.speaker: Donald Trump, US President-elect (Truth Social post)
a6368.speech: Trump celebrated the soon-to-be-announced agreement in a posting on his Truth Social social media platform: “WE HAVE A DEAL FOR THE HOSTAGES IN THE MIDDLE EAST. THEY WILL BE RELEASED SHORTLY. THANK YOU!”

a6368.speaker: Israel (government)
a6368.speech: Israel says it has killed around 17,000 militants — though it has not provided evidence to support the claim. It also blames Hamas for the civilian casualties, accusing the group of using schools, hospitals and residential areas for military purposes.

a6368.speaker: South Africa (allegations before the International Court of Justice)
a6368.speech: The International Court of Justice is investigating allegations brought by South Africa that Israel has committed genocide.

a6368.speaker: International Criminal Court (arrest warrants)
a6368.speech: The International Criminal Court, a separate body also based in The Hague, has issued arrest warrants for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his defence minister and a Hamas commander for war crimes and crimes against humanity linked to the war.

a6368.speaker: Israel and the United States
a6368.speech: have condemned the actions taken by both courts.

a6368.speaker: Israeli authorities
a6368.speech: Israeli authorities have already concluded that more than a third of the roughly 100 remaining people held captive are dead, and there are fears that others are no longer alive.

a6368.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister
a6368.speech: has vowed to continue the war until Hamas’s military and governing capabilities are destroyed. ; Netanyahu has said Israel will maintain open-ended security control over Gaza as well as the occupied West Bank, territories captured by Israel in the 1967 war that the Palestinians want for their future state.

a6368.speaker: Israel (government)
a6368.speech: Israel has said it will work with local Palestinians not affiliated with Hamas or the Western-backed Palestinian Authority.

a6793.speaker: Mary Njoroge, Representative of the World Food Programme (WFP) Djibouti
a6793.speech: In her opening speech expressed her gratitude to the partners who made the vocational training programme in transport and logistics possible, namely MENFOP, ONARS, MASS, UNHCR and USAID; indicated that upstream the United States Embassy and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) took the gamble of financing the vocational training programme in order to fight poverty and that this would have a direct impact on “Zero Hunger” in Djibouti; “This shows boldness and produces positive results” ; explained that the partnership between the stakeholders had enabled the development of training courses intended to be as inclusive as possible, notably to strengthen gender equality and the inclusion of refugees and out-of-school Djiboutians; testified that she has faith in this programme and hopes the certificates delivered today will trigger the employment opportunities Djibouti offers as a regional logistics hub ; “WFP, in support of the Government of Djibouti, continues and pursues its objective of fighting hunger, whether through food assistance to the most vulnerable families or through vocational training.”

a6793.speaker: Mohamed Abdallah Mahyoub, Secretary General of the Ministry of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a6793.speech: Said he was delighted to take part in this event, which in his view symbolizes a successful partnership with a multitude of actors (WFP, MENFOP, ONARS, MASS, USAID); assured the officials of the various partners present of his joy at having joined this noble operation and at the support the Minister of National Education, Mr. Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, continues to give to vocational training in Djibouti; did not conceal his satisfaction at seeing refugee children take part in the training and receive certificates; recalled that the credit goes to the Head of State, who in 2016 committed to integrating refugees into national structures, and affirmed that this is a national satisfaction and a source of pride; said in conclusion that the continuation of this programme remains a challenge and that it is necessary to act together with a view to the integration and granting of decent work for these young people.

a6793.speaker: Houssein Hassan Darar, Executive Secretary of the National Office for Assistance to Refugees and Disaster Victims (ONARS)
a6793.speech: After reviewing the advantages of these training courses, urged the young people to do honour to their families and relatives, and also to demonstrate to all the partners who supported this training that their investments had led to a happy outcome and a complete victory.

a6793.speaker: Martha Dye, acting Representative of USAID
a6793.speech: Declared that this programme, carried out by WFP and financed by the American government through USAID, made it possible to join the efforts made by the Djiboutian government to respond to the challenges of the labour market and to offer an opportunity to young Djiboutians, particularly the out-of-school and refugees, so that they can be competitive in the job market; indicated that the creation of these training courses testifies to the will to develop human capital in the most efficient and inclusive way possible ; “This programme also testifies to the development that Djibouti has experienced over the last two decades and I am convinced that with a workforce better adapted to supply, Djibouti will be a leading commercial and logistics hub” ; praised the achievement of this first graduating class and encouraged the graduates to continue on this path so as to be the future actors of the region's development and masters of their own destiny.

a6896.speaker: SADC Anti-Corruption Effort Index pilot report
a6896.speech: The pilot report highlighted significant progress, notably in legal reforms, stakeholder engagement and political will of which is key to sustainable anti-corruption reform.

a6896.speaker: Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Tanzanian Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a6896.speech: Said that in addressing the corruption vices within the region, there is need to push for the adopting of new approaches like the established Regional Anti-Corruption Effort Index successfully piloted by Tanzania and Mauritius ; “To address the corruption vice, Member States have made steady progress in the implementation of the SADC Anti-Corruption Strategies Action Plan and also continue to place emphasis on adopting new approaches such as development of a Regional Anti-Corruption Effort Index of which two countries namely the Republic of Mauritius and the United Republic of Tanzania have already been piloted.”

a6896.speaker: Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Tanzanian Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a6896.speech: Remarked that the region has continued to do commendable work in enhancing peace and security through collaboration among Member States in which structures like Early Warning Systems and the Panel of Elders are essential in these efforts ; He expressed gratitude to the Elders Panel and the Mediation Reference Group for their support towards regional conflict resolution and mediation initiatives ; He said the establishment of the Network of Women Mediators will help to address the needs of women and children in the peace process, ensuring that no one is left behind.

a6896.speaker: Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Tanzanian Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a6896.speech: Said there is a strong commitment to combat terrorism in the region, through enhanced collaboration and capacity building at the Regional Counter Terrorism Centre located in Dar es Salaam.

a6896.speaker: Mahmoud Thabit Kombo, Tanzanian Minister for Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
a6896.speech: On democratic governance feats, said the region remained committed especially with four Member States that have conducted elections ensuring successful transition of power ; He also assured the SADC Electoral Observation Mission (SEOM) of Tanzania’s peaceful and smooth election ahead in October.

a6896.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a6896.speech: In his introductory remarks encouraged the Member States to remain resolute and stand in solidarity regarding the changing geopolitical developments with the rising tariffs, barriers and declining of foreign aid which impacts the region.

a6896.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a6896.speech: On transnational crimes such as poaching, illicit drugs, human trafficking, cybercrime, arms proliferation and motor vehicle theft, said SADC Police Chiefs have reaffirmed their commitment to address the problem.

a6896.speaker: Elias Magosi, SADC Executive Secretary
a6896.speech: Reiterated SADC unwavering commitments to the Democratic Republic of Congo, despite the diplomacy engagement in conflict resolution, the region will continue to oversee to ensure DRC achieve lasting peace.

a7053.speaker: High-level panel on food systems in protracted crises (participants)
a7053.speech: They emphasised that a truly sustainable food system is more than just its individual sectors—it is an interconnected network that must consider people, the environment, and the broader ecosystem.

a7053.speaker: Dr. Björn Niere, Head of Cooperation at the German Embassy in South Sudan
a7053.speech: “A sustainable food system puts people at the center – as producer, processor or consumer. It ensures food security and nutrition for all by taking a holistic approach” ; “It will respect the economic, social and environmental bases to generate food and nutrition for future generations.
